headline: Roman has new evening confusion, with the stove left on once, plus a weight loss of about 8.6% since Sep 5 and a decline in bathing and dressing independence.

items.statement: On 2026-11-09 his niece Linda reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, including once leaving the stove on. He was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The nurse's plan was urinalysis, medication review and a PCP visit that week. No encounters are recorded in the period, and no results are documented in the notes provided.
items.verifier_note: The 11/09 nursing note matches every detail: two weeks of evening confusion, the stove, orientation, no fever, and the plan. The encounters record is empty, which supports the statement that no encounters are recorded.

items.statement: Weight fell from 82.3 kg on 2026-09-05 to 75.2 kg on 2026-11-24, a loss of 7.1 kg (8.6%). Readings were 79.8 kg on 10/01 and 77.3 kg on 10/28. On 11/24 the dietitian noted poor appetite, skipped breakfast and about 50% of day center lunches eaten. The plan is an oral supplement twice daily, weekly weights and a dental check.
items.verifier_note: The vitals record gives all four weights and the -7.1 kg (-8.6%) change. The dietitian note supports the appetite, breakfast and 50% lunch findings and the plan. The note rounds the loss to 9%, which is consistent with 8.6%.

items.statement: On 2026-09-18 Roman needed hands-on help out of the tub and said he has been skipping showers because he fears slipping. On 2026-09-25 OT found he now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing; he was independent at the last review. OT recommends a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: The 9/18 aide note and the 9/25 OT note support every detail, including the prior independence and all three recommendations.

questions_for_team: Have the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on 11/09 been completed, and what were the results? Should the medication review also consider the weight loss?
Could the evening confusion and the stove incident affect safety at home while he is alone, and what supports are needed?
Are the OT recommendations (tub transfer bench, handheld shower, more bathing hours) ordered and in place? Who is following up?
How will the weight loss and poor intake be monitored, and when will the weekly weights and dental check happen?
The Oct 19 fall entry was corrected as a charting error, but the 10/24 PT evaluation refers to that fall. Should the PT plan be verified to confirm it belongs to Roman?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters, ED visits, urgent care visits, and hospital admissions in that window; note any chest pain, dyspnea, or COPD exacerbation presentations given ischemic heart disease and chronic obstructive bronchitis.
Falls and fall-related injuries: check for any falls, near-falls, or fractures in the window, given age 74, chronic pain, fibromyalgia, and knee osteoarthritis.

Medication reconciliation: compare the active list (metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, naproxen, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin) against the last review; flag any new starts, stops, dose changes, or refill gaps, especially for clopidogrel and metoprolol adherence.

Review naproxen use in context of ischemic heart disease, hypertension, and anemia: check for new NSAID-related concerns, any bleeding or GI symptoms, and recent hemoglobin or CBC results, and flag for prescriber review rather than recommending a change.

Anemia and bleeding surveillance: review most recent hemoglobin/hematocrit trend, iron studies if on file, and any bleeding events, since he is on dual antiplatelet-type therapy (clopidogrel plus NSAID).

Blood pressure trend: pull all recorded BP readings in the window, check for hypotension or persistently elevated readings relative to the hypertension diagnosis and beta-blocker use, and note any orthostatic symptoms.
Weight and BMI trend: compare weights across the window against prior review given obesity (BMI 30+), prediabetes, and metabolic syndrome; flag change of 5 percent or more.
Glycemic monitoring: review most recent HbA1c and fasting glucose results and any new diabetes diagnosis or medication start, given prediabetes and metabolic syndrome.
Lipid and cardiac follow-up: check whether lipid panel is current on simvastatin 20 mg, and confirm any cardiology or ischemic heart disease follow-up visits and nitroglycerin spray use frequency.

Pain, function, and ADLs/IADLs: assess chronic low back pain, fibromyalgia, and knee osteoarthritis pain scores, mobility, ADL and IADL changes, and whether pain is interfering with function or sleep; check cognition and mood screening (PHQ/GAD) and social engagement, plus caregiver situation and any care-plan items due in the window (for example reassessment dates, advance directive review, and COPD action plan review).
